title: prompt/confirm must pass the prompt's last character to the input function (readline workaround) and must not add or strip characters

note.title: prompt/confirm must pass the prompt's last character to the input function (readline workaround) and must not add or strip characters
answers: click.prompt with prompt_suffix="" shows an extra trailing space
why does part of my prompt go to stdout when err=True
backspace clears the whole prompt line with readline
how does click.termui split the prompt between echo and input
note.body:
Symptom: with `prompt_suffix=""`, `click.prompt`/`click.confirm` rendered an extra trailing space ("bar" became "bar "); earlier, without the workaround, readline backspace cleared the whole line (#665, #2092).
Root cause: src/click/termui.py:prompt (inner prompt_func) and src/click/termui.py:confirm used `echo(text.rstrip(" "))` and then `f(" ")`, which rewrote the prompt and always added a space.
Fix pattern: echo everything except the last character (`echo(text[:-1], nl=False, err=err)`), then hand exactly `text[-1:]` to the input/getpass function (`f(text[-1:])` / `visible_prompt_func(prompt[-1:])`). The rendered prompt must be exactly the text plus the suffix, with nothing trimmed or appended.
Constraints: this split is intentional. With `err=True`, the prompt minus its last character goes to stderr and the last character goes to stdout (e.g. `prompt("bar", prompt_suffix="", err=True)` sends "ba" to stderr and "r" to stdout). Don't "fix" this by moving everything to echo, because that brings back the readline backspace bug. tests/test_utils.py checks the exact stdout/stderr split with capfd for prompt and confirm, with and without a suffix, so update those asserts together with any change here.
note.applies: Any change to prompt rendering in src/click/termui.py prompt() and confirm()
